title: Potala Palace: 2,300 Tickets a Day, One Hour Inside | China Travel Expert
description:
The Potala Palace in Lhasa is one of the hardest big sights in China to actually get into. Daily entry is capped at about 2,300 visitors, it stands at roughly 3,700 metres, and once you're inside you get about one hour — the interior visit is strictly timed.

So this is a book-ahead, show-up-on-time kind of place: miss your allotted slot and that's it. Add the altitude (give yourself a couple of days in Lhasa to acclimatise first) and the one-hour clock, and a little planning is the difference between a smooth visit and a wasted trip.

🧭 Expert Tip: book your Potala entry days ahead — peak months (roughly May-October) sell out — and spend 2-3 days acclimatising in Lhasa before you climb.
